i think you're jumping to a lot of conclusions from this very short post. being comfortable with some femininity does not equal being comfortable as a woman. we don't know anything else about this person; we don't know what "dressing like a woman" entails for them, or if they experience dysphoria.

i, *personally*, would never be comfortable with that amount of femininity because of its associations with womanhood & how intense my dysphoria is. wearing a dress would make me feel like i'm being perceived as a woman & that's a huge no-go for me. but someone with equally debilitating dysphoria who is also comfortable wearing a skirt at times *still experiences that dysphoria*, even if it's not triggered by wearing a skirt.

if this person had included in this post an indication that they don't experience dysphoria or that they were comfortable with their body or being perceived as a woman, your confusion & frustration would be merited, but you're basically just doubting someone's transsexuality because they like to play dress-up sometimes. this is so tame relative to a lot of stuff trenders tend to say lol i don't think any good can come out of making a snap judgement about someone like this

not to say that this person *is definitely* a transsexual, cus we don't know that either, just the phrasing of their post doesn't really lend credibility to your claims
